**Head of Engineering Job Description:** Scope, Impact & Qualifications Reports to: CEO Level: Executive (CTO-equivalent scope) Org size: ~25 engineers Time split: 70% Product / 30% Discipline ROLE SUMMARY The Head of Engineering owns the technical outcomes of Maestro's entire product suite while also serving as the top of the engineering discipline ladder: every engineering manager and individual contributor ultimately ladders up to this role. The position deliberately splits attention: 70% product execution, 30% discipline accountability. Product delivery is the immediate, ongoing accountability; discipline work compounds over time and requires protected but smaller blocks of focus so it doesn't get crowded out by delivery pressure. This role sits at the center of Maestro's matrix structure, accountable for craft quality and standards company-wide, while ensuring embedded engineering talent on each product team is pointed at the right priorities.
  
  
**SCOPE • Org reach:** all engineering leads across all product lines report into this role (directly or via a lead layer), the senior-most engineering accountability in the company. • Product surface: full product suite, every active product line's engineering output. • Discipline surface: engineering-wide standards, tooling, and process, independent of which product team an engineer sits on. THE 70%: PRODUCT ACCOUNTABILITY The Head of Engineering is the single accountable owner for engineering execution across Maestro's product portfolio.
  
  
**What this looks like day to day:** • Partners with the engineering leads of every product line to ensure their teams are resourced against the right priorities: not just busy, but correctly sequenced. • Accountable for ensuring product strategy and roadmap direction are translated into clear, actionable engineering plans, serving as the connective layer between Product and Delivery leadership and the engineering organization, primarily through engineering leads embedded within product teams. • Accountable for applying technical judgment to turn high-level strategic priorities into concrete technical execution plans, enabling and guiding engineering leads to scope, sequence, and de-risk delivery across their product areas. • Identifies where product priorities and engineering capacity are misaligned across teams and resolves the tradeoff, including cross-team resourcing calls.
  
  

* Is the escalation point when a product line's engineering execution is off track, and is accountable for getting it back on track. Impact: Every product line ships against strategy, not just against what's easiest to build. Product and Delivery leaders have one accountable engineering partner instead of negotiating separately with each product line's lead. THE 30%: DISCIPLINE ACCOUNTABILITY The Head of Engineering owns what "good engineering" means at Maestro, independent of the product line.

**What this looks like day to day:** • Sets and maintains company-wide engineering standards (code quality, architecture principles, technical debt posture). • Owns cross-cutting technical initiatives that no single product team should solve independently, e.g. product suite services and universal QA automation. • Defines how AI tooling is used across engineering, including guardrails to ensure AI usage improves output quality and velocity rather than introducing risk or degrading craft.
  
  

* Identifies and removes friction in how engineering work gets done company-wide, streamlining processes that slow every team down in the same way. • Is the ultimate accountable owner for engineering management practice (how EMs lead, how performance is evaluated, how the craft is grown) even where day-to-day people management is embedded in product teams. Impact: Engineering quality, velocity, and management practice don't fragment by product line. An engineer's experience of "how we build software here" is consistent no matter which team they're on, and the org gets the benefits of scale (shared tooling, shared standards) instead of each team reinventing its own.

SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE • Engineers across the organization deliver flawless technical execution that earns long-term client retention and supports growth. • Product lines are resourced against strategic priority, with tradeoffs made explicitly rather than by default. • Engineering leads across product lines operate with a shared technical bar and shared tooling. • Company-wide initiatives (QA automation, AI usage standards) ship and get adopted, not just get designed.
  
  

* Engineering management practice is consistent and healthy across the org, even though EMs are embedded in product teams day to day. QUALIFICATIONS Maestro hires for demonstrated capability, not years-of-service checkboxes. The bar below is competency-based: what someone needs to be able to do, not how long they've been doing it. Required competencies: • Has personally carried end-to-end accountability for engineering delivery across more than one product or team simultaneously: not just led a single team, but balanced competing priorities across several.
* Can translate ambiguous, high-level strategy (from product, business, or leadership) into a technical execution plan that engineers can actually build against, without needing someone else to do that translation. • Has designed or materially improved an engineering standard, process, or tooling investment that worked across teams (not a single-team fix) and can point to the before/after. • Comfortably operates in a matrixed environment, influencing and aligning engineering leads, their teams, and cross-functional stakeholders without relying on formal authority. • Has hands-on technical depth sufficient to earn credibility with senior engineers and to personally evaluate technical tradeoffs.

This is not a purely managerial role. • Has direct experience managing or mentoring engineering managers, not only individual contributors. • Demonstrates sound judgment on when to standardize company-wide versus when to let product teams operate with autonomy. Strongly preferred: • Experience operating at this scope inside a company of comparable size (roughly 15 to 50 engineers), where formal process is lighter and judgment calls happen more often than policy lookups.
  
  

* Direct experience setting a company's approach to AI-assisted engineering (tooling choices, guardrails, or usage standards) rather than just using AI tools personally. • A track record of building or scaling QA automation, testing strategy, or release process across multiple teams. • Experience partnering directly with Product and Delivery leadership as a peer, not just receiving requirements from them. • Experience leading engineering for always-on, customer-facing digital products or live-service platforms, where availability, release discipline, observability, incident response, and rapid cross-functional coordination directly affect the end-user experience and client retention.

**What we're explicitly not requiring:** • A specific prior title (VP Engineering, CTO, etc.). We care about scope actually carried, not the title it came with. • A minimum years-of-experience threshold. Competency and evidence of impact matter more than tenure.
  
  

* Deep expertise in every technology in Maestro's stack. Technical judgment and the ability to evaluate tradeoffs matter more than hands-on fluency in any one language or framework.

**Position Title:** EMS Education Manager

As one of the largest and most comprehensive public health organizations in the nation, we are at the forefront of research and innovations to improve the efficacy of public health statewide, nationally, and internationally.

PHI was distinguished as one of the top 50 “Best Non-Profit Organizations to Work For” by the Non-Profit Times in a national search.

  

##### **POSITION SUMMARY**

The Bridge Center (Bridge) at the Public Health Institute (PHI) works across the health care system to expand access to low-barrier addiction treatment and sexual and reproductive health care, and to advance health equity. Since 2019, CA Bridge has supported more than 290 hospitals to implement medications for addiction treatment (MAT) in the emergency department (ED) based on the CA Bridge model for 24/7 low-barrier access to evidence-based care. Since then, Bridge has trained teams in 22 states, 56 EDs, and 6 EMS agencies. Collectively, they reach 2,181 providers whose EDs see nearly 2.5 million patient visits a year.

EMS Bridge extends low-barrier MAT to paramedics, bringing EMS-initiated buprenorphine to communities across the country, including in California. The National Expansion Project builds capacity for emergency department-based MAT across the country; the ED Syphilis/HIV/HCV Screening Program supports emergency departments in implementing routine opt-out screening and linkage to care; and Access Bridge increases access to contraception and treatment for pregnancy emergencies from the ED.

##### **POSITION OVERVIEW**

Bridge is hiring an EMS Education Manager to work with our EMS Bridge team. EMS Bridge began in California, which remains home to our largest EMS program and much of our ongoing EMS research and implementation work, and now supports EMS agencies in other states. The EMS Education Manager will lead day-to-day planning, coordination, and delivery of EMS Bridge education, training, and technical assistance for paramedics, EMTs, and EMS educators, training officers, and agency leaders. Additionally, this role will lead the development and ongoing improvement of EMS Bridge curricula, run EMS Bridge learning collaboratives, and support grant reporting on training and technical assistance activities. Strong project management expertise will be necessary in these tasks. The successful candidate will bring direct experience as a paramedic or EMT and as an EMS educator and will work with a range of team members and external partners to support EMS agencies to offer buprenorphine and connection to ongoing care for people with opioid use disorder.

The full salary range for this position: $79,333 to $115,098 per year. The typical hiring range for this position is from $79,333 (minimum) to $97,216 (midpoint). The starting salary is determined based on the candidate’s knowledge, skills, experience, and budget availability.

Employment Type: Full Time

##### **Important Information**

* This is a regular full-time 1.0 FTE position with a schedule of 40 hours per week.
* This is a fully remote position that requires travel approximately 30% of the work time, to EMS agency sites, trainings, conferences, and partner meetings as requested, including 2-4 All Staff meetings per year in the San Francisco Bay Area.
* The selected candidate will determine their work schedule in collaboration with their supervisor and is expected to be available during core business hours (9:00am – 2:00pm Pacific Time). Some trainings may be scheduled outside core hours, requiring flexible availability, to reach EMS crews on varied shift schedules.
* This position is open to applicants nationwide.
* **To apply, please submit a resume and cover letter detailing your interest in and qualifications for this position.**

##### **ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES include the following:**

##### **EMS Training & Technical Assistance**

* Under the direction of the National & EMS Program Director, lead the planning, coordination, and delivery of trainings for paramedics and EMTs, in person and virtually, including initial buprenorphine trainings, refreshers, case reviews, and scenario-based sessions.

  + Developing agendas, learning objectives, session plans, facilitation approaches, and supporting materials for collaborative learning activities.
  + Identifying and coordinating Bridge staff, clinical consultants, field providers, and external presenters to contribute to learning collaborative sessions and other educational programming.
  + Incorporating equity and harm reduction content throughout collaborative programming.
  + Fostering opportunities for paramedics, EMTs, and EMS educators to learn from one another and build professional connections across agencies and regions.
* Partner with EMS educators, training officers, and agency leaders to build their capacity to teach EMS Bridge content within their own agencies.

* Assess the training and technical assistance needs of field providers and participating agencies and identify appropriate strategies, resources, and subject matter experts to address those needs.
* Alongside other members of the EMS Bridge team, provide technical assistance related to implementing EMS-initiated buprenorphine, including protocol rollout, field workflows, documentation, patient engagement, crew buy-in and addressing stigma, and handoffs and linkage to care with emergency departments and community treatment programs.
* Identify common themes, challenges, and emerging needs surfaced through trainings, mentorship, and collaborative activities and communicate those findings to Bridge leadership to inform future programming and resource development.
* Identify and disseminate promising practices, tools, resources, and emerging evidence relevant to EMS-initiated buprenorphine and prehospital overdose response.
* Track participation and capture feedback and testimonials from trainings, site visits, and learning collaboratives.
* Represent the Bridge Center’s EMS training and technical assistance work at meetings, trainings, EMS conferences, and other events as requested.

##### **Curriculum & Educational Resource Development**

* Under the direction of the National & EMS Program Director, support development, adaptation, and ongoing improvement of EMS Bridge training curricula and educational resources for paramedics, EMTs, and EMS educators.
* Develop practical, accessible training materials and resources, including presentations, facilitator guides, case scenarios, skills and simulation activities, job aids, quick-reference tools, and other educational products.
* Collaborate with Bridge clinical experts and other subject matter experts to translate clinical guidance and evidence into practical educational materials for field providers.
* Coordinate subject matter expert review of curricula and resources to ensure materials are accurate, relevant, consistent with Bridge’s approach, and appropriate for EMS audiences.
* Support processes for offering continuing education credit for EMS Bridge trainings, where applicable.
* Incorporate participant feedback, implementation experience, emerging evidence, and changes in the EMS and substance use care landscape into ongoing curriculum and resource improvements.

##### **Project Management & Reporting**

* Manage the day-to-day implementation of assigned EMS training, technical assistance, learning collaborative, and curriculum-development activities from planning through completion.
* Maintain and support the development of project workplans, timelines, milestones, and deliverable trackers to ensure activities remain on schedule.
* Collect and synthesize training attendance, evaluation results, participant feedback, and lessons learned to inform continuous quality improvement.
* Support grant reporting by preparing training and technical assistance data, narratives, and site summaries in line with funder deliverables.

Perform other duties as assigned.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.

* Five years’ work experience, including at least one year of experience as a paramedic or EMT, and experience teaching or training others in EMS and/or other clinical settings
* Bachelor’s degree; or high school diploma and an additional four years of relevant work experience, or associate’s degree and an additional two years of relevant work experience.

***Vision***: Every child in Indiana thrives in a safe, loving, forever home.

The Family Case Manager represents DCS and supports families in a local or central DCS office. **About Tides**
===============

Tides is a nonprofit and philanthropic organization committed to advancing social justice. We work across the social sector to shift power to communities of color and other groups historically denied power.

Centering equity and justice in everything we do, we collaborate in deep partnership with movement leaders, nonprofits, donors, foundations, and corporations to amplify the impact of their work by providing services like fiscal sponsorship, donor advised funds, grant making, and a variety of innovative solutions. Learn more at tides.org.

**About this Role**
===================

Tides seeks a strategic, experienced, and mission-driven leader to serve as its Vice President, People & Culture. The Vice President will be responsible for the culture, systems, and talent that make Tides’ work for its partners and communities possible.

This is a pivotal moment for the organization as Tides responds to external pressures and seeks greater impact through innovation with minimal workforce growth. Meeting these demands will require more of Tides’ people practices: thoughtful organizational design, clear goals and performance expectations, modern, well-integrated systems, and a culture that helps staff adapt to change with confidence. The Vice President will shape how Tides’ staff works, collaborates, and adapts, sustaining the best of Tides’ mission-driven, remote-first culture while strengthening accountability, goal setting, performance management, and organizational effectiveness.

Reporting to the Chief Legal and People Officer, the Vice President will be a trusted advisor to Tides’ senior leaders on workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, culture, change management, and JEDI principles and practices. Tides seeks a leader who pairs trust, care, and inclusion with candor and accountability; who can move fluidly between long-term strategy and day-to-day execution; and who will ensure that Tides’ people practices reflect its values and power its mission. The role carries a broad scope and real complexity. The Vice President will lead the people agenda across Tides Network and Tides Center, including an HR team providing support for Tides’ fiscally sponsored projects. They will also serve, in collaboration with the President & CEO and the Executive Team, as an architect and custodian of Tides’ culture, translating the organization’s values into everyday behaviors and keeping a remote-first workforce connected to the mission and to one another.

Reporting to the Chief Legal and People Officer, the Vice President, People & Culture is responsible for shaping Tides’ workplace culture, scaling its organizational infrastructure, and optimizing the end-to-end employee experience across Tides Network, Tides Center, and Tides Foundation, balancing strategy with tactical execution and ensuring that day-to-day people operations are aligned with organization-wide goals.

The Vice President has responsibility for all people functions, including employee and labor relations, organizational development, people operations, talent acquisition, and total rewards. The role also oversees HR business support for Tides Center’s fiscally sponsored projects and Tides’ workforce development, performance management, and staff safety and security. The Vice President will work closely with fellow senior leaders and department heads to ensure alignment between strategy and day-to-day needs and operations.

The Vice President will lead the People Team, with direct reports that include: the Director, Total Rewards & People Operations; the Director, Organization Development and People; and the Director, Tides Center People.

As an executive leader, the Vice President must execute duties and responsibilities while embracing and exhibiting Tides’ core competencies: Leading Self, Leading People, Leading Results.

  

**What you will Do**
====================

**People Strategy**
-------------------

* Serve as a strategic advisor to executive and senior leadership on workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, culture, engagement, change, and emerging people priorities.
* Develop and lead Tides’ People & Culture strategy, aligning people priorities with organizational strategy, financial realities, and future workforce needs.
* Help shape and steward Tides’ culture, translating organizational values into leadership practices and day-to-day behaviors.

**Culture & Organizational Effectiveness**
------------------------------------------

* Lead organizational design, change, leadership development, succession, performance management, engagement, and other efforts that strengthen organizational effectiveness and employee experience.
* Build a culture of trust, inclusion, accountability, transparency, continuous learning, healthy feedback, and operational excellence, embedding JEDI principles throughout the organization’s practices and decisions.
* Drive workforce and talent strategy, including workforce planning, recruiting, onboarding, and retention, in partnership with Finance, Strategy, Legal and other organizational leaders.

**People Team Leadership**
--------------------------

* Lead and develop a high-performing team, establishing clear priorities, service standards, accountability, and strong partnership across the organization.
* Manage the department budget and oversee performance, talent development, operations, and succession planning.

**People Operations**
---------------------

* Provide strategic direction and oversight for compensation, benefits, job architecture, career pathways, HRIS, payroll partnerships, and other people operations, ensuring programs are equitable, competitive, compliant, and financially sustainable.
* Ensure People Team policies, programs, and practices comply with employment, benefits, and labor laws and the Collective Bargaining Agreement, in partnership with Legal, Risk & Compliance and Finance.
* Champion the thoughtful use of technology and AI to modernize people practices, strengthen the employee experience, and improve efficiency and service delivery.

**Internal Communications & Enterprise Initiatives**
----------------------------------------------------

* Execute internal communications operations in coordination with the Vice President, External Affairs & Strategic Communications, ensuring effective and aligned communication across Tides.
* Lead and coordinate cross-functional initiatives that advance workforce, culture, and broader organizational priorities.

**What you will Bring**
=======================

* 10+ years of directly applicable senior business and HR leadership experience and a relevant bachelor’s degree, or 12+ years of relevant experience, including at least six years in senior leadership roles in-house partnering with executives and leading senior teams;
* Significant experience leading the people function in a complex, matrixed, multi-entity organization, with broad expertise across organizational effectiveness, talent and leadership development, workforce planning, performance management, total rewards, employee and labor relations, talent acquisition, and HR operations;
* Experience aligning labor strategy with business goals including operational excellence and financial sustainability while building a constructive, collaborative labor relationship in support of a healthy organization.
* A track record of leading organizational change and transformation, translating people strategy into measurable outcomes and using data and KPIs to assess impact.
* Strong enterprise, business, and financial acumen, with the ability to connect workforce and people strategies to organizational, operational, and fiscal priorities.
* Experience advising executive leadership and Boards on complex workforce, organizational, and people matters.
* A demonstrated commitment to culture, engagement, inclusion, and belonging, including experience engaging and connecting a remote-first workforce.
* Exceptional judgment, communication, and influencing skills, with the ability to navigate complexity, challenge constructively, resolve conflict, build alignment, and make difficult decisions with clarity and empathy.
* An authentic, collaborative, and low-ego leadership style, characterized by high emotional intelligence, accountability, approachability, and comfort operating in a dynamic environment.
* Strong operational and technology orientation, with experience strengthening systems, processes, and HR technology and an openness to emerging tools, including AI; and
* Experience in a substantially unionized environment.

**Preferred qualifications include:**

* Nonprofit or philanthropic experience, particularly experience spanning nonprofit and for-profit environments;
* Advanced degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Business Administration, or a related field; and
* SHRM-SCP, SHRM-CP, or another relevant HR certification.

Title: Director of Commercial Shared Services
Description:
### **Job Purpose**

The Director of Commercial Shared Services leads the shared commercial capabilities that support Arabic AI Agents & Services verticals. The role is responsible for ensuring the effective integration and performance of Sales Development Representatives (SDR), Bidding, and Sales Operations, establishing consistent processes, governance, reporting, and service standards across the commercial pipeline. Working closely with the COO and the Heads of AI & Agents and Services, the Director translates commercial priorities into coordinated lead-generation, bid-management, and operational-support activities; improves pipeline visibility and execution; and enables the commercial teams to pursue opportunities efficiently, consistently, and in line with company objectives.

### **Shared Commercial Strategy & Governance**

* Translate the Commercial priorities into an integrated operating plan for SDR, Bidding, and Sales Operations, supporting both the AI & Agents and Services verticals.
* Establish shared commercial processes, standards, service levels, and ways of working that promote consistency while accommodating the distinct requirements of each vertical.
* Define clear ownership, handover points, and escalation routes across lead generation, opportunity qualification, bid/no-bid decisions, proposal development, CRM administration, and commercial reporting.

### **Leadership & Performance Management**

* Lead, coach, and develop the Heads and Managers within the shared commercial functions, setting clear expectations, priorities, and accountability.
* Agree function-level objectives and KPIs, review performance regularly, address gaps, and ensure corrective actions are implemented.
* Plan and allocate resources across SDR, Bidding, and Sales Operations according to agreed commercial priorities, workload, deadlines, and business needs.
* Promote collaboration, knowledge sharing, continuous improvement, and a results-oriented culture across the shared services teams.

### **Sales Development & Pipeline Support**

* Oversee the SDR function’s lead-generation and prospecting plans, ensuring targeting, qualification criteria, outreach activity, and meeting generation align with the priorities of both commercial verticals.
* Define and oversee the SDR strategy, including lead-generation approaches, target-account prioritization, prospecting channels, and outreach strategies, ensuring alignment with the commercial and go-to-market objectives of both verticals.
* Drive the adoption of AI-enabled tools and automation within SDR activities to enhance lead identification, research, qualification, outreach personalization, and follow-ups, while automating routine tasks such as CRM updates, lead enrichment, and reporting to improve productivity, scalability, and operational efficiency.
* Ensure effective lead handover and feedback loops between SDR and the relevant AI & Agents or Services business development and account management teams.
* Review lead-generation and pipeline-contribution results with the Head of SDR, using data and market feedback to improve lead quality, conversion, and productivity, and continuously optimize SDR strategies, processes, AI utilization, and automation effectiveness against relevant performance KPIs.

### **Bidding & Proposal Management**

* Oversee the bidding function to ensure opportunities are assessed, prioritized, and managed through a disciplined bid lifecycle, from qualification and bid/no-bid decisions to submission and post-submission follow-up.
* Develop and oversee the bidding strategy, including opportunity prioritization, bid/no-bid decisions, resource allocation, and win strategies, ensuring alignment with commercial objectives, GTM priorities, and market opportunities.
* Ensure bids and proposals are coordinated with the relevant vertical and subject-matter teams, are responsive to client requirements, and meet quality, compliance, commercial, and submission-deadline requirements.
* Position the Bidding function as a strategic business partner by engaging relevant functions, including Business Development, Presales, Product, Engineering, Production, Finance, Legal, and Marketing, early in the bid lifecycle to jointly shape opportunities, develop competitive proposals, and maximize win probability.
* Drive the adoption of AI-enabled tools and automation across the bidding lifecycle to improve opportunity assessment, RFP analysis, requirement mapping, proposal development, and content reuse, enhancing efficiency, quality, and scalability while maintaining appropriate accuracy and compliance controls.
* Monitor bid pipeline, submission schedules, win/loss outcomes, and lessons learned; use insights to strengthen bid strategy and proposal effectiveness.
* Escalate material bid risks, resource constraints, pricing or margin considerations, and approval requirements to the appropriate decision-makers.
* Build and continuously develop a scalable bidding and proposal management capability by strengthening team capacity, competencies, tools, and processes to support increasing bid volumes, complex opportunities, and the commercial growth of both verticals.

### **Sales Operations, CRM & Commercial Reporting**

* Oversee Sales Operations activities, including CRM governance, data quality, pipeline reporting, sales dashboards, forecasting support, commercial documentation, and process administration.
* Ensure commercial data, opportunity stages, activity records, and reporting definitions are consistent and reliable across the AI & Agents and Services verticals.
* Provide the COO and commercial leadership with timely analysis of pipeline health, lead conversion, bid performance, workload, and other relevant commercial KPIs.
* Develop and maintain a centralized Commercial Hub that supports both AI & Agents and Services while ensuring clear differentiation in their market positioning, value propositions, offerings, and commercial messaging.
* Oversee the maintenance of sales enablement materials, proposal and presentation templates, commercial collateral, and relevant records and workflows, ensuring the development of tailored presentations, sales decks, and marketing collateral that reflect the distinct value propositions and commercial priorities of each vertical while maintaining consistent corporate branding.
* Drive the effective use and continuous improvement of CRM platforms and other commercial tools, coordinating adoption, user guidance, and process changes as needed.
* Ensure the Commercial Hub operates as a strategic enabler for both verticals by facilitating access to commercial resources, standardizing best practices, and supporting the development and continuous improvement of sales enablement materials and tools.

### **Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Management**

* Work closely with the Heads of AI & Agents and Services to understand their priorities, coordinate shared-function support, and resolve competing demands transparently.
* Partner with Finance, Legal, Marketing, Production, Technology, Products and other relevant teams to support forecasting, budgeting, proposal development, contract coordination, and compliant commercial execution.
* Maintain clear communication with stakeholders on priorities, capacity, deadlines, risks, performance, and required decisions.
* Ensure shared services support both verticals fairly and effectively, with priorities and resource allocation based on agreed business needs.

### **Process Improvement, Risk & Compliance**

* Document, maintain, and improve shared commercial workflows, policies, procedures, templates, and controls.
* Identify bottlenecks, duplication, data gaps, and operational risks across the commercial process, and implement improvements that increase efficiency and quality.
* Ensure activities within the shared commercial functions comply with company policies, approval authorities, contractual requirements, and applicable regulatory obligations.
* Promote the use of performance data, stakeholder feedback, and lessons learned to continuously improve service quality and commercial outcomes.
* Carry out other duties necessary for the effective operation of the department.

  
**Requirements**  

### **Education, Experience & Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Management, or a related field; a relevant postgraduate qualification is an advantage.
* 12-15 years of relevant experience across commercial operations, sales operations, bidding/proposal management, sales development, or related commercial functions, including substantial leadership experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading multiple teams or functions, setting performance expectations, and improving processes and operational effectiveness.
* Strong understanding of commercial pipelines, lead generation and qualification, bid management, CRM governance, sales reporting, and forecasting support.
* Experience using CRM platforms such as Salesforce or HubSpot, sales analytics and reporting tools, and Microsoft Office applications.
* Familiarity with SDR, lead-generation, and bidding/proposal management platforms is an advantage.
* Experience in technology solutions and product companies is an advantage; experience in AI companies is a strong advantage.
* Excellent command of written and spoken English; Arabic proficiency is an advantage.
